questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following molecules shows an increase in bond order after loss of an electron from the highest occupied molecular orbital?
questions.solution: Bond order is given by $\dfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$. If an electron is removed from an antibonding molecular orbital, $N_a$ decreases, resulting in an increase in bond order. If it is removed from a bonding molecular orbital, $N_b$ decreases, resulting in a decrease in bond order. The molecular orbital electronic configurations are: $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{*2} \pi_{2p_y}^{*2}$ The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) is $\pi_{2p}^{*}$, which is antibonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_a$, increasing the bond order from $1$ to $1.5$. $\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2}$ The HOMO is $\sigma_{2p_z}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $3$ to $2.5$. $\text{C}_2$ (12 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2}$ The HOMO is $\pi_{2p}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $2$ to $1.5$. $\text{B}_2$ (10 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{1} \pi_{2p_y}^{1}$ The HOMO is $\pi_{2p}$, which is bonding. Loss of an electron decreases $N_b$, decreasing the bond order from $1$ to $0.5$. Thus, only $\text{F}_2$ shows an increase in bond order. Answer: $\text{F}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the order of bond energy between C=S $\ $ C=Te, and between Cl–Cl $\ $ F–F?
questions.solution:
The bond energy of C=S is greater than that of C=Te because the $2p$-$3p$ orbital overlap in C=S is more effective than the $2p$-$5p$ orbital overlap in C=Te. As the size of the bonded atom increases, the extent of overlap decreases, leading to a weaker bond.

The bond energy of Cl-Cl is greater than that of F-F. Although F is smaller and expected to form a stronger bond, the extremely small size of the F atom results in strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the two bonded F atoms. This repulsion weakens the F-F bond compared to the Cl-Cl bond.

Thus, C=S > C=Te and Cl-Cl > F-F.

Answer: C=S > C=Te and Cl–Cl > F–F
